points.t: Dry, cracked, scaly or blistering hands; worse with work, cold or frequent washing.
**Irritant** barrier breakdown ± delayed **allergy**; atopy lowers the threshold.
Emollient after every wash, soap substitute, lined gloves, **potent steroid** in short bursts.
Eczema herpeticum, infection, occupational disease, and tinea manuum treated as eczema.

cause.lead: Wet work strips the barrier; allergy may join in.
points: **Irritant**: wet work, detergents, solvents, cement, friction, occlusive gloves → ↑ water loss, barrier failure.
Small repeated insults add up (**cumulative ICD**) → thickening and lichenification.
**Allergic** (type IV): chromate, rubber accelerators, preservatives, fragrance, acrylates, epoxy.
A damaged barrier makes sensitisation easier, so **ICD and ACD often coexist**.
Modifiers: atopy / filaggrin loss, winter, hot water, dominant-hand exposure.
**Acute**: redness, vesicles on finger sides and palms, oozing.
**Chronic**: scale, hyperkeratosis, lichenification, painful **fissures**, nail ridging.
**Irritant clues**: finger webs, ring site, dorsal hands, dominant hand worse.
**Allergic clues**: matches contact sites (glove cuff, fingertips with acrylates); better on holiday.
**Hyperkeratotic palmar**: thick fissured central palms, little itch; mimics psoriasis.

visuals.caption: Irritant wet-work pattern (left): dry, red, fissured skin over the finger webs, knuckles and under a ring. Pompholyx (right): deep ‘tapioca’ vesicles along the sides of the fingers and across the palm.
visuals.alt: Two hands showing irritant hand eczema and pompholyx

items.name: Chronic irritant
items.t: Dry, fissured, glazed; webs and ring site.

items.name: Pompholyx
items.t: Recurrent crops of deep, very itchy vesicles; peels in 2–3 weeks.

items.name: Infected
items.t: Crusting, weeping, pain: swab and treat.

points: Job tasks, **wet work** (> 2 h/day or > 20 washes/day), gloves, products (safety data sheets).
Better at weekends or on holiday?
Both hands, nails, wrists.
**Always the feet** (tinea, pompholyx, psoriasis), scalp and elbows.
Any **asymmetric** or treatment-resistant scale: mycology for tinea manuum.
All chronic hand eczema (> 3 months) or suspected ACD.
Read D2 and D4 (± D7); judge **relevance**.

cards.name: Palmoplantar psoriasis
cards.clue: Sharp margins, thick silvery scale, nails.

cards.name: Tinea manuum
cards.clue: ‘Two feet, one hand’; white scale in creases.

cards.name: Keratolysis exfoliativa
cards.clue: No itch, no redness; air-filled peeling collarettes.

cards.name: Scabies
cards.clue: Burrows in webs and wrists; night itch; contacts.

manage.lead: Protection + adequate steroid + maintenance. Steroid alone relapses.

points: Reduce or replace irritants and allergens.
Right gloves, **cotton liners**, short occlusion; remove rings for wet work.
Lukewarm water, soap substitute, dry webs; emollient after every wash and overnight.

rx.drug: Potent TCS (mometasone 0.1% or betamethasone valerate 0.1% ointment)
rx.note: Then twice-weekly proactive maintenance on usual sites.
Taper; review every 4 weeks; dorsal skin thins easily.

points: Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment (off-label) as steroid-sparing maintenance.
Potassium permanganate 1:10,000 soaks for weeping or vesicular phases.
Treat infection: swab; flucloxacillin or as local guidance.
Not controlled after ~4–6 weeks optimised TCS, chronic > 3 months, or uncertain.
Specialist: **delgocitinib 2% cream** (NICE TA1107), **alitretinoin** (NICE TA177; Pregnancy Prevention Programme), phototherapy, systemics.

limits.t: Do not treat eczema; sedating one at night only for sleep.
No substitute for gloves and emollients.
Severe acute flares only, under specialist advice.

items.t: Painful punched-out erosions or sudden worsening: **eczema herpeticum**.
**Work-related**: occupational health, document exposures, patch-test referral.
One-sided scaly hand + tinea pedis: **scrape before steroids**.

pearls.t: One fingertip unit covers both sides of one hand.
Always look at the **feet** in a hand rash.
Glove-cuff cut-off on dorsal hands and wrists: think glove allergy.
Healthcare: alcohol rub when not soiled, dry fully before gloving, emollient at breaks.
Don’t advise quitting the job early: modification often succeeds.

quiz.a: Lasting more than 3 months, or relapsing at least twice a year despite adequate treatment.
Tinea manuum (with tinea pedis): take scrapings before steroids.

quiz.q: Typical first-line steroid for a hand eczema flare?
quiz.a: A potent TCS ointment (e.g. mometasone 0.1%) once daily for 2–4 weeks, then twice-weekly maintenance.
All chronic hand eczema (> 3 months) or suspected allergic contact dermatitis.

quiz.q: Painful punched-out erosions on eczematous hands?
